p.i: Te rege tuti rura ferat labor Magnus coloni, per mare nauita[?] Currant quietum, Faustitasque Aurea spargat opes benignas. Vindex auaras destrue fortior Fraudes, vaganti frena licentiæ Repone, cædes & scelestas Pœna comes premat usque culpas. Sic regna magnis regibus obtine Rex maior, uno rite minor Deo. Sic laude venturi decorum Perpetua celebrent nepotes.

Sic te Cœlituum pater Cunctis incolumem seruet ab hostibus, Et nostris precibus fauens Pergat sacrilegæ gentis, & hospitæ, Iuratas caput in tuum Dextras fulmineo rumpere brachio: Vt rex sceptra rebellibus Tandem perdomitis Gallica temperans Pacis dulcia Candidæ Plebi restituas otia subdita.

page.notes: The word "nauita" is only partly clear in the scan; it may be "nauitæ". The top verse passage is set as two stanza blocks; the line breaks follow the printed lines. Long s has been normalised to s throughout.
